_note: Batch 9, derived in RUNBOOK order. Two notes carried in deliberately: glossary_deep_research spends real web-search money, so its card is raised and NEVER approved — the gate is the evidence, not the spend. propose_edit declares NO synonyms at all, which per R2 makes it unreachable through answerability; it is a frontend tool advertised on the editor surface, so the scenario runs there and the surfacing question is asked explicitly rather than assumed.

scenarios.prompt: Start composing this book — set up the authoring workspace for it.
scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: it is NOT idempotent — its own description says 'create (or get, idempotently)', and the harness fixture already mints a composition Work during provisioning, so this turn must resolve to the SAME work rather than a second one. Read composition_work for this book: more than one row is the defect. CONTROL: the fixture creates the work at build time, so a turn reporting 'created' is not automatically wrong — the row count is what settles it.

ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — the headline property: calling twice must return one work, not two.

scenarios.prompt: Research Aldric Vane on the web and find sources for him.
scenarios.prompt_source: _meta.synonyms['research this on the web'] + ['find sources for this character'].

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: The entity must exist, because the tool takes an entity_id — the model has to resolve the NAME to that id, which is the step that has failed twice in this loop (kg_propose_edge, world_map_create).

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: it spends web-search money with NO confirm card — this is a PAID tool and the gate is the whole audit. EXPECTED LIVE OUTCOME is a card, left unapproved, store unchanged. 🔴 THE CARD IS NEVER APPROVED IN THIS SCENARIO: approving it buys real web searches, and the LIVE bar is satisfied by reaching the tool, not by paying. Also REFUTED IF the model invents an entity_id rather than resolving 'Aldric Vane' — that is the D-DECLARED-UUID class again and must be recorded as a new instance.

ship_audit.gate: The card IS the audit — a paid web call with no gate would be the defect.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — an entity_id that does not exist must be refused before anything is bought.

scenarios.prompt: How many jobs do I have — give me the counts by status.
scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a read-intent turn changes the store, OR the reply states counts without jobs_summary being called — jobs_list carries the rows and a count assembled from a truncated listing is the registry-vs-live shape again. CONTROL: batch 7 measured jobs_list returning 10 running jobs for this account, so a summary reporting ZERO active would contradict a known reading and is a finding either way.

ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — an account with no jobs must report zeros, not an absence of the answer.

scenarios.prompt: Run the next compiler pass on my plan — do the cast pass.

args.source_markdown:
# The Ember Codex

## Arc 1 — The Hollow Keep
- Chapter 1: Aldric reaches the Hollow Keep and is given the Codex.
- Chapter 2: Mira Solene warns him the Codex is read by more than one reader.

wait.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM plan_artifact pa JOIN plan_run pr ON pr.id=pa.run_id WHERE pr.book_id='{book_id}' AND pa.kind='spec'
wait.why: plan_run_pass needs a run_id AND a pass_id, and a run has neither until the async spec job lands. Batch 5 measured what happens without this wait: 'no spec to compile', 3/3, which reads as a tool defect and is a fixture that was not ready.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM plan_artifact pa JOIN plan_run pr ON pr.id=pa.run_id WHERE pr.book_id='{book_id}' AND pa.kind='spec'
seed_assert.why: The SPEC is the precondition, not the run — an assertion that cannot fail in the way the scenario fails is not an assertion.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: it runs a pass out of dependency order (the description says the seven passes run in order — motifs, cast, world, beats, chapters, …), OR it reports a pass complete while plan_artifact gains no row for it. CONTROL: the model must obtain run_id from the store (composition_package_tree), which is the chain plan_compile used in batch 5 — a turn that invents one is the D-DECLARED-UUID class.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — an unknown pass_id must be refused with the closed set, not defaulted.

scenarios.prompt: Make the opening line of this chapter darker — show me the change before it goes in.
scenarios.prompt_source: NO _meta.synonyms are declared for this tool at all. That is itself the finding to check: per R2, answerability cannot reach it, so it is on the wire only because it is a FRONTEND tool advertised on the editor surface. The prompt is therefore ordinary editing prose, and the scenario runs WITH editor_context so the surface is the one where it lives.
scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the chapter body CHANGES — propose_edit shows an Apply button and must never write by itself; the store diff is the whole test. Also REFUTED IF the turn ends claiming the edit was made rather than proposed (the D-NARRATED-WRITE shape, which this tool is uniquely able to produce). CONTROL: it declares no synonyms, so if it is NOT surfaced the finding is about the frontend-tool advertisement path, not about answerability.

ship_audit.gate: The Apply button IS the gate — the proposal must reach the user unapplied.
ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — a proposal identical to the current text should be refused or reported as a no-op, not shown as an edit.
ship_audit.tenancy: n/a by construction — it edits the chapter open in the caller's own editor.
